answer: Min-cut conductance gating: each agent’s routable capacity is set by the minimum conductance cut separating its service-dependency neighbors from diverse existing communities (lotus partitions). A pearl threshold marks sufficient external diversity; dense internal-only clusters with thin external cuts (mesa-shaped components) are throttled. Sybil rings can cheaply add internal edges, but raising the min-cut requires many real cross-community service dependencies, forcing attackers to maintain costly heterogeneous peer links.
